records.claim: The pseudocode looks up usefulness in a single UT table and uses a single hash function for all three WT tables.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: The figure explicitly defines three separate usefulness tables whose outputs are summed, and three separate hashes (h0, h1, h2) for the weight tables.

patch.value:
sR_sum = 0
ut_row = UT0[skew(PC)] + UT1[skew(PC)] + UT2[skew(PC)]
for bank in 0..7:
  valid_regs = {r | r % 8 == bank and RegisterDigestTable[r].valid}
  if valid_regs is empty: continue
  best_r = argmax_{r in valid_regs} ut_row[r]
  if ut_row[best_r] > 0:
    digest = RegisterDigestTable[best_r].payload[11:0]
    bank_pred = WT0_bank[h0(PC, digest)] + WT1_bank[h1(PC, digest)] + WT2_bank[h2(PC, digest)]
    sR_sum += bank_pred * sR_multiplier
return sR_sum

value.name: extract_fp_bits
value.trigger: Called by generate_digest for FP types
value.pseudocode:
if class == FP64: return V[63:55] << 3
else if class == FP32: return V[31:26] << 3
else if class == FP16: return V[15:13] << 3
value.notes: Uses the exact bit ranges from Figure 6(b) instead of abstract exponent/sign functions.
